name: Chooz Reactor Neutrino Site

operator.note: No source fetched this session states an explicit operator distinct from the Double Chooz Collaboration and EDF (which operates the adjacent Chooz Nuclear Power Plant, not the experimental site itself).

intervals.label: hosting Double Chooz
intervals.quote: located at 1050 m from the reactor cores of the Chooz nuclear power plant in France
intervals.note: No official facility page was reachable this session to independently source a facility-level founding/operating interval; start is the same inferred lower bound used for experiment:double-chooz's earliest interval. The site remains a candidate host for other reactor-neutrino work (e.g. the cevns workstream's NUCLEUS) beyond Double Chooz's own 2017 shutdown, so `end` is left null rather than closed.

notes: The Double Chooz official site (double-chooz.fr, doublechooz.in2p3.fr, chooz.in2p3.fr) was unreachable (DNS failure) on every domain guessed this session; this record relies on the 2012 arXiv discovery paper, INSPIRE, and Wikipedia.
This id (`facility:chooz`) is also referenced by the cevns workstream for the NUCLEUS experiment, per the Wave 3 ID_REGISTRY; created here exactly as specified.

summary.plain: The site near the Chooz nuclear power station in northern France where the Double Chooz experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from the reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site adjacent to the Chooz-B nuclear power plant, Ardennes, France, hosting the Double Chooz near (400 m) and far (1050 m) detector halls.
